summary: editable-contracts preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute an obfuscated sibling payload
details: The npm package advertises itself as a mobx-based React form-editing library, with its library code living in dist/editable-contracts.js. However, package.json declares a preinstall hook that runs setup.mjs, which downloads a standalone Bun runtime binary from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip, extracts it to a temporary directory, marks it executable, and invokes it via execFileSync against the ~730KB sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is heavily obfuscated using an obfuscator.io-style string-array plus rotator (n7gIxM string array, WV8StW rotation function, mangled _0x hex identifiers) and is not referenced by the package's main entry or README. setup.mjs itself is lightly obfuscated (e.g. _0x488df8 aliasing fs, _0x9e5ce7 constructing the Bun download URL). The advertised library entry point is unrelated to the preinstall behavior; the alternate runtime is fetched solely to execute an opaque blob under a runtime the package does not otherwise use. This is an alternate-runtime dropper: on npm install, an unrelated interpreter is retrieved and used to run smuggled, obfuscated code on the installer's host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
